thread:
anya: quick sync — noticed cross-tenant tail latency spikes when small-alloc workloads run alongside large-embed jobs. looks like slab fragmentation is the suspect.

matt: yep saw that in traces. small allocs end up on 64KB slab pages and we waste a lot of host memory waiting for compaction.

liam: can you paste a short repro? which models / shapes?

anya: mostly embedding workers (64-dim, lots of short lived tensors) + sparse attention traces. repro on a dual-tenant ded pool with 8 GPUs.

anya: snippet from the allocator stat dump:
```
slab_size: 65536
free_chunks: 1200
small_allocs: 1.7M
avg_live_per_slab: 48
tenant_tags: [A,B]
```

hao: rough idea — either reduce slab granularity for the small allocator (eg 4KB slabs) or switch to per-tenant slab isolation with slow cross-tenant slurp/compaction. both have costs.

matt: reduction means more metadata overhead and more GPU page table entries, maybe worse for large tensor throughput. per-tenant isolation wastes memory but isolates tail-latency.

liam: tradeoff matrix we should consider:
- small slab: +better packing for tiny tensors, -more allocations/pagewalks, +less compaction pressure
- tenant pools: +predictable latency per tenant, -hard to pack when tenant is idle, -requires CIDR-like partitioning of pool capacity

anya: also think about compaction coordination. today compaction runs opportunistically on the host and migrates pages across slabs which adds spikes. could we do background draining with IO-smoothing?

hao: background drain sounds good but requires safe point for GPU kernels touching those buffers. we have to ensure KV cache invariant across copies. that implies a small quiesce protocol:
1) mark slab as draining
2) reject new allocations into slab (or redirect)
3) wait for active refs to drop (or move/refcount)
4) memcpy pages off-device and update mappings

matt: that increases allocation latency in the short path if we check drain marks. maybe push checks into a fast bit-test in the allocator hot path.

liam: can we do a hybrid: keep 64KB default but carve a small 10% of pool as 4KB micro-slab region for tiny alloc bursts? experiments would be quick.

anya: I like that. minimal risk. we can add a runtime knob: `SMALL_SLAB_POOL_PERCENT=10` and track `tiny_alloc_hit_rate`.

anya: proposed experiment plan:
- create micro-slab pool at 8% and 16% configs
- run mixed tenant repro for 1h windows, measure p50/p95/p99 alloc latency and per-tenant tail gen latency
- add metric `micro_slab_eviction_count` and `cross_tenant_compactions`

hao: also add histogram for `slab_reuse_distance` so we can see fragmentation dynamics.

matt: one more thought — for per-tenant guarantee we need admission control at RPC layer so a tenant can't consume all micro-slabs causing noisy neighbor. that ties into our router quotas though.

liam: agree. for now keep micro-slab shared with soft fairness (token bucket) and let Dedicated hosts reserve micro-slab for tenants with guarantees later.

infra-bot: scheduled: eng-runtime/allocator-experiment-169999 -> starts 2023-11-15T10:00:00Z, duration 2h. :robot_face:

anya: thanks infra-bot. I'll add the experiment PR with benchmarks and dashboards.

matt: can you also add a quick perf test for pagewalk overhead when slab size changes? I want numbers for TLB / mmap walk cost.

anya: yes, adding `tools/alloc_bench.py --slab-size=4096|65536` to the runbook.

hao: if experiment shows good tiny alloc hit rate we can fold micro-slab into allocator mainline with a toggle and add an A/B rollout. else fallback to per-tenant isolation RFC.

liam: sounds good. action items: anya -> PR + dashboards; matt -> pagewalk perf test; hao -> metric defs and compaction tracepoints.

anya: noted. will post PR link and raw numbers back here when ready. :thumbsup:
